transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Holt (Redwood Product), Marta Ruiz (HarborSat VP Product), Ethan Park (HarborSat Platform Eng), Sana Iqbal (HarborSat Security), Noah Lim (HarborSat DevOps)

Summary:
Quick technical handoff for marketplace connector and orchestration model. Discussed Helm operator pattern, KMS integrations, VPC connectivity, on-prem/air-gap packaging, and an initial benchmarking plan. Identified next steps for runbook, manifests, and credentials for test tenant.

Topics:
- Listing packaging: container artifacts, helm chart, certs, marketplace metadata
- Networking: VPC peering, NAT, egress control, marketplace connector VPN vs direct peering
- Security: KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs, RBAC mapping
- Performance: expected QPS, p99 latency targets, GPU node sizing, autoscaling policies
- Rollouts: canary A/B, fallback to hosted model variants, quantization compatibility

Action items (also in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick around the table, um, so we have liam and priya from Redwood, marcus is on product, and from HarborSat Marta, Ethan, Sana and Noah. 
[00:12] Marta Ruiz: great thanks, uh, excited to get this off the ground, we've got some internal deadlines for marketplace listing early Q1 so want to align on the tech checklist.
[00:22] Priya Kapoor: awesome, we'll walk through the helm operator pattern, what we expect for K8s, plus the runtime bits (basically the sidecar router and the model serving pool). there's a sample repo we can share.
[00:33] Ethan Park: quick question up front, our infra is multi-az on EKS, we also have an air-gapped edge cluster for sensitive customers — how much of the listing package has to be modified for air-gap?
[00:45] Priya Kapoor: good call, um, the core should be the same, but for air-gap we provide tarball of container images + offline helm index — you'll need to run our offline bootstrap script. We also have an operator that handles cert rotation, but if you want HSM integration that's a little extra config.
[01:05] Sana Iqbal: when you say HSM, do you mean Redwood calls into our KMS or do you expect the connector to hold keys? we need audit logs and key separation.
[01:15] Priya Kapoor: Redwood doesn't retain customer keys in hosted mode for the dedicated/private option you'll manage keys — we integrate with customer KMS via a key-ref pattern; for on-prem or private we give you config to point at your HSM or cloud KMS. audit logs are emitted from the operator and we can push them to your Splunk/ELK via a sidecar.
[01:35] Noah Lim: (murmur) if you can push to our existing ELK that's ideal, we don't want to stand up a separate pipeline.
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: yep, that's supported. we'll include fluentbit config in the repo.
[01:45] Marcus Holt: quick product note — for a marketplace listing we need a versioned helm chart plus an operators.yaml and a small images manifest, plus a listing metadata file that describes required permissions, supported regions, and minimal node size.
[02:00] Marta Ruiz: okay, what's minimal node size for typical gen-2 models at 2k context? we need a cost estimate for customers.
[02:10] Priya Kapoor: uh, ballpark, for 2k tokens you'd want one p4-like (or a 48g A100 equivalent) per model replica if you need <100ms p50 and p99 under 500ms depends on batching. but there's a lot of knobs — quantized variants can run on 16g GPUs at lower throughput.
[02:35] Ethan Park: so we should expect variable instance types; does Redwood support autoscaling across heterogeneous node pools?
[02:45] Priya Kapoor: yes, our runtime supports heterogeneous pools and smart routing. you can set node selectors in the helm values and the operator will route requests to compatible variants, and we have fallback policies — eg if high-precision node pool is saturated it can hit a quantized variant.
[03:05] [crosstalk — multiple speakers] 
[03:12] Liam Chen: one wrinkle on marketplace listing is the billing and metering contract — we need to ensure the metering hooks are exposed and the connector emits usage events to the marketplace billing endpoint. Marcus, do we have a sample payload?
[03:26] Marcus Holt: yes, we'll share the metering schema; it's basically per-token + embedding units plus a few flags for private-call vs hosted-call. we'll put a sample webhook in the repo.
[03:38] Marta Ruiz: on the security side, our legal wants SOC2 alignment and a record of where data persists. what does Redwood do for data residency and audit histories?
[03:50] Priya Kapoor: for hosted we persist transient tokens and KV cache for speed but not logs; for private/dedicated, data stays in your VPC and we can configure retention. we'll provide audit log export and the SOC2 report; for the listing we'll include a compliance package.
[04:10] Sana Iqbal: can we toggle token retention off? some customers require zero retention.
[04:18] Priya Kapoor: yes, retention toggle is supported in config — you can set session retention to 0 and disable caching. performance will be impacted obviously.
[04:28] Ethan Park: what's the process for E2E test runs? we want to run a benchmark with our traffic profile.
[04:34] Liam Chen: we do bench runs in a dedicated test tenant — Redwood will spin up a test cluster or you can run locally and point at our test control plane. we should coordinate a 2-hour run to capture p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization.
[04:50] Noah Lim: for the cluster, we prefer to size for the 99th percentile for a pilot; we'll share historical traffic and sequences.
[04:58] Priya Kapoor: perfect. please include the sequence length distribution and concurrent requests per second; that helps us set batching window defaults.
[05:10] Marta Ruiz: any network requirements? for marketplace listing do we need NAT egress or open ports?
[05:18] Priya Kapoor: minimal egress to Redwood control plane over TLS (443) for metrics and heartbeats. For private deployments you can opt for an outbound-only model via proxy; if you want inbound peering we support a VPN/peer connection but that adds ops complexity.
[05:35] Ethan Park: our security shows deep packet inspection and egress filtering; will the operator work with those policies?
[05:42] Priya Kapoor: yes, the operator only needs to egress to the specific endpoints; we can provide IP ranges and FQDNs. we'll also sign our container images — we recommend attestation via Cosign for image provenance.
[06:00] [15min jump in transcript for brevity] 
[20:12] Priya Kapoor: walking through the helm values file, there's a section for kmsProviders, RBAC mappings, and marketplace metadata. note the marketplace metadata requires region codes, supported runtimes (e.g., k8s v1.26+), and the minimal required kube roles.
[20:28] Ethan Park: can we map the marketplace listing to our internal entitlement service? we need SSO mapping to our groups.
[20:36] Marcus Holt: we support SAML and OIDC and you can pass group claims to the operator — operator will map groups to RBAC roles. we'll add an example for Auth0 and Okta in the repo.
[20:50] Marta Ruiz: pricing — do we declare pricing slabs in the listing or negotiate per-customer?
[20:56] Liam Chen: marketplace listings usually include a recommended price but enterprise deals can override. we do metering so billing integration is flexible.
[21:05] Sana Iqbal: about audit logs, retention windows — our compliance folks need 7 years for some customers, is that feasible?
[21:13] Priya Kapoor: technically yes — logs can be exported to your long-term storage, but we'd advise storing aggregated events rather than full transcripts for cost. we'll document retention knobs.
[21:30] Ethan Park: on quantization — do you have recommended models/quant profiles we should list as supported?
[21:36] Priya Kapoor: yes we'll include a compatibility matrix. some model variants are only supported on fused-kernel backends, so we'll put compatibility notes per model.
[21:50] Noah Lim: anything special for updates/rollbacks in the marketplace? how do we push a patch without breaking running customers?
[21:57] Priya Kapoor: operator supports canary and live traffic shadowing; you can configure rollout percentages and automatic fallback if error rate spikes. plus version pinning in the listing metadata so customers can opt-in to new versions.
[22:15] [short silence — notes being typed] 
[22:21] Marta Ruiz: all right, this is helpful. next, logistics: test tenant, repository access, and the benchmark.
[22:29] Liam Chen: I will create the test tenant and share credentials. Priya will drop the helm repo, manifests, and sample metering webhook. Marcus will add the listing metadata template.
[22:42] Ethan Park: i will gather the traffic profile and sample sequences and send to liam.
[22:46] Sana Iqbal: I'll pull the compliance matrix and confirm SOC2 scope items.
[22:52] Priya Kapoor: one more thing — if you plan to use the private package for on-prem, expect an additional packaging step for air-gapped customers; we can provide a script to sign and import images.
[23:05] Noah Lim: good to know. any gotchas?
[23:08] Priya Kapoor: sometimes the main gotcha is assumptions about persistent KV cache across restarts — we recommend using a PVC backed cache or external redis for durability. also, the marketplace may require extra metadata for billing reconciliation so don't omit the customer id mapping.
[23:28] [overlap] Marta Ruiz: are there rate limits we should advertise?
[23:33] Liam Chen: in hosted mode we publish per-route rate limits; for dedicated/dedicated-private you set quota in the listing. we'll include a default in the metadata.
[23:45] Marcus Holt: I'll follow up with a draft listing metadata doc by end of day Friday (2026-11-27).
[23:52] Marta Ruiz: excellent. thanks all.
[23:55] Liam Chen: recap / next steps: repo + helm by priya 11/30, cluster sizing from ethan 11/26, test tenant creds by liam 11/25, compliance list from sana 11/27, and schedule bench during week of 11/30.
[24:15] Marta Ruiz: that works. thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
